$comment: RELEASE PARITY STATE. Enforced by scripts/release-parity-check.ts, which runs in CI and before a release. This file records, for every canonical migration at the release frontier, whether it is believed applied on the hosted database, and which database objects it introduces. The guard fails when application code on this branch references an object whose migration is not applied -- the exact class of failure that stopped employers saving jobs during UAT. It NEVER connects to a database, holds no credentials and applies no migration; it compares this repository against itself. Edit it deliberately: every entry is an owner-level statement about production.

frontier.note: EXPAND half of a two-phase release; the application half is 20261008090000 + the Career Journey code, which must NOT merge before this is applied. Consolidates the self-reported current profession into ONE canonical home: before this, security_career_profiles.current_profession_slug and sp_passport_profiles.cig_profession_slug were both user-writable, from two surfaces, with nothing keeping them in step. Adds a reconciliation log with least-privilege grants: SELECT on the table, COLUMN-LEVEL UPDATE (resolved_at) only, no INSERT and no DELETE, and an explicit REVOKE first because Supabase default privileges would otherwise grant all of them including TRUNCATE. Column-level because RLS constrains rows, not columns: a table-wide UPDATE would let a holder rewrite the canonical/passport values, the resolution or created_at on their own audit row, reconciles the existing rows under a rule that never overwrites a user own answer, and installs three sync triggers: canonical -> Passport mirror, seed of a newly created Passport row, and a temporary COMPATIBILITY trigger carrying an old client Passport write back to the canonical row. BACKWARD COMPATIBLE BY CONSTRUCTION: no column is dropped, no constraint is added that an existing client could violate, and the current application keeps writing exactly what it writes today -- proven statement-for-statement in Group F of supabase/tests/canonical_professional_profile_test.sql (54 assertions, full replay green). Safe to merge and apply with current main still running.
frontier.verify: SELECT s.user_id, s.current_profession_slug, p.cig_profession_slug FROM public.security_career_profiles s JOIN public.sp_passport_profiles p ON p.holder_user_id = s.user_id WHERE s.current_profession_slug IS DISTINCT FROM p.cig_profession_slug;

frontier.note: CONTRACT half. Drops the temporary compatibility trigger 20261007090000 installed, once no client writes sp_passport_profiles.cig_profession_slug any more. Introduces no object, so it creates no code dependency and never blocks an application release. ORDERING: ships in the SAME PR as the application phase and is applied AFTER it is live. That happens naturally -- Lovable rebuilds from origin/main at merge, so the new code is running before anyone can apply this file. Applying it early is premature rather than dangerous (old Passport writes would stop reaching the canonical row and the two copies could diverge again, exactly as they do on main today); applying it late costs nothing, because the trigger simply never fires. Verified locally against the 54322 stack: expand -> contract -> re-apply -> rollback all succeed, and the rollback reopens a WORKING compatibility path.

frontier.note: Hosted owner UAT P0: a recruiter saved a rating and could not change it. Introduces no object. It makes scp_interview_assessments_superseded_by_fkey DEFERRABLE INITIALLY IMMEDIATE and replaces scp_iv_record_assessment so the original row is marked superseded BEFORE the replacement is inserted. The old order put two live rows in scp_interview_assessments_live_idx for the duration of the INSERT, so every attempt to supersede an assessment failed on a raw unique-violation -- the supersede path could never have worked, and had no test. Behaviour-only: no column, no table, no policy and no grant change; the unique index, the locked guard, the in-place-edit guard, the reattribution guard and the confirmed-evidence rule are all untouched, and the evidence rule is now asserted against the supersede path too (R2.17h). Order-independent with the UI: the server function has passed a supersede reason through since it was written, so this only makes a call that was already being made succeed. Verified locally against the 54322 stack -- full db-test.sh replay green, 85 Interview Intelligence runtime assertions including save -> reopen -> edit -> save.

Observed on public.cv_documents: 14 columns; relrowsecurity = t; exactly four policies, all TO authenticated -- own cv select (USING auth.uid() = owner_user_id), own cv insert (WITH CHECK auth.uid() = owner_user_id), own cv update (USING and WITH CHECK auth.uid() = owner_user_id), own cv delete (USING auth.uid() = owner_user_id); no employer, recruiter, reviewer or admin read policy. relacl = {postgres=arwdDxtm/postgres,service_role=arwdDxtm/postgres,authenticated=arwd/postgres} -- authenticated holds SELECT/INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE only, service_role holds ALL, and there is NO anon and NO PUBLIC grant and no TRUNCATE for authenticated, i.e. the REVOKE-then-GRANT block took effect. Indexes: cv_documents_pkey (id) and cv_documents_owner_recent_idx on (owner_user_id, updated_at DESC). Trigger cv_documents_set_updated_at is present as a BEFORE UPDATE FOR EACH ROW trigger executing public.set_updated_at(). Foreign key cv_documents_owner_user_id_fkey REFERENCES auth.users(id) ON DELETE CASCADE. Row count 0 -- schema half only, no application writer in this release, consistent with the schema-first release contract. Verification was read-only: no row, no auth configuration, no key, no regulatory baseline and no other ledger entry was modified.

frontier.note: SCHEMA HALF of the AI CV. Private, owner-only storage for saved CV documents: presentation over facts that stay in security_career_profiles, sp_experience_periods, sp_claims and profiles, plus a snapshot of those facts so a saved CV does not silently change when the profile does. NO application code references cv_documents in this release -- that is the schema-first release contract working as designed, and schema-first-release-check asserts it. The save/load code becomes merge-eligible once this is recorded applied. Owner-only RLS with four separate policies (WITH CHECK on insert and update, so a row cannot be created for or reassigned to another person); privileges REVOKEd from PUBLIC/anon/authenticated first and re-granted to authenticated only, because Supabase default privileges otherwise ship anon INSERT/DELETE/TRUNCATE on any new table; anon gets nothing. No share token, no public column, no recipient table: a CV carries employment history and credentials and needs its own access model rather than the Career Card's. Writes no assertion_level, lifecycle_state, verified_at or verified_by_user_id -- it can create no verification. Verified locally: full db-test.sh replay green against the 54322 stack, including the 24 cv_documents assertions in supabase/tests/cv_documents_privacy_test.sql.
